questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles concurrent changes to a customer's credit balance? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two threads call apply_to_invoice for the same customer and the same invoice at the same time, with a 500 cent balance and a 300 cent invoice. What is the result?
choices: Both deduct 300 and the balance goes to -100
Both return 0 because the balance is locked
The second raises because the invoice was already applied
The first deducts 300; the second returns the recorded 300 without deducting again

questions.prompt: Two requests for a customer who has never been seen both call _account() simultaneously. Why can't they end up with different _Account objects?
choices: The dictionary's get method is atomic and blocks others
The lookup, creation and insertion all happen while holding _accounts_guard
Each _Account has its own lock so duplicates are harmless
CPython serializes all method calls on one object

questions.prompt: InvoiceFinalizer calls gateway.charge() after apply_to_invoice has returned, not inside it. What is the main reason this matters?
choices: It lets the gateway see the credit-adjusted amount
It guarantees charge() runs at most once
A slow or hung network call does not keep the customer's credit lock held, so other credit operations for that customer proceed
It prevents reverse() from deadlocking with apply_to_invoice
